first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this because she can't decide whether to use a travel agent or one of these honeymoon planners, and we're putting money towards it. I read it top to bottom on the iPad. The opening is refreshingly honest: they're just labels, so compare what each one actually does. Good. It's calm, no silly slang, and it's full of the questions I'd ask anyway: whose name is on the booking, whose terms apply, what's in writing, what happens if the business goes under. It doesn't make me feel old-fashioned for asking them. My trouble is the same as always: the page tells me to ask who looks after them in the middle of the night, and whether the business holds insolvency insurance, and then doesn't answer either question for Wedded Wonderland itself. And I'd want to know a phone call comes first.

journey.quote: In practice both are labels rather than defined titles, and many businesses use more than one of them.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that, and I appreciate being told straight. Our old travel agent in Camberwell would never have admitted it.

journey.quote: Put the same questions to anyone you are considering, ask for the answers in writing and set them side by side.
journey.reaction: Exactly how Geoff and I would do it. In writing, side by side.

journey.section: Questions about what they will actually do
journey.quote: Then ask whether they receive anything from the suppliers they recommend, and whether that is disclosed to you.
journey.reaction: That's the first thing Geoff will ask. Glad it's said openly rather than hidden.

journey.section: The same questions, side by side
journey.quote: | Ask a planner | Ask an agent | Why it matters |
journey.reaction: I went down the table looking for the difference between the two columns and there isn't one. Every row says the same thing twice. I see the point, ask both the same thing, but on the iPad it's a lot of repeated text, and I wondered for a moment if I'd misread it.

journey.section: The same questions, side by side
journey.quote: What will you book, and in whose name?
journey.reaction: Good. Who holds each booking is who's responsible, and that's what I want pinned down.

journey.section: Questions about how they are paid
journey.quote: Will the quote be in Australian dollars, with your fee shown separately from the trip?
journey.reaction: Yes. AUD and the fee shown separately. That's what I'd want before we transfer a cent.

journey.section: Questions about how they are paid
journey.quote: The [guide to sending money overseas](https://moneysmart.gov.au/banking/sending-money-overseas) sets out what to compare.
journey.reaction: A Moneysmart link. Sensible, and a government source I trust.

journey.section: Questions about what happens when plans change
journey.quote: An agent or intermediary is usually bound by the provider's terms and, legally, may only need to pass on the remedy that provider offers.
journey.reaction: That's useful and a little sobering. It's the sort of thing nobody tells you until it's gone wrong.

journey.section: Who do we contact while we are away?
journey.quote: Ask for a name, a contact method and the hours, and whether you call the business, the airline or the hotel first if something goes wrong in the middle of the night at home.
journey.reaction: That is my question, almost word for word. I'll be looking to see how Wedded Wonderland answers it.

journey.section: What does our travel insurance need to cover?
journey.quote: Insolvency insurance is not compulsory for agents, so ask whoever you book through whether they hold it.
journey.reaction: This is the deposit question. Good advice, but it tells me to ask and then the Wedded Wonderland section doesn't say whether they hold it. Also, the word 'deposit' never actually appears, and that's what I'm worried about.

journey.quote: Honeymoon-only planning follows the same Wedded Advisor process.
journey.reaction: The bullets just below help: Wedded Concierge seems to be the service and the Wedded Advisor the person. But this sentence on its own is jargon. Plain words, please.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact.
journey.reaction: A named person who stays with us. That's what I want to hear.

journey.quote: Your advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: AUD, good. But 'your time zone' is Melbourne. The article asked who picks up in the middle of the night, and when the children are in Greece that's the question. It isn't answered here.

journey.quote: Tell your Wedded Advisor about the wedding, the honeymoon and the feeling you want, agree the fee in writing before any work begins, and see each inclusion on paper before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing before any work, inclusions on paper. Sensible. 'Start with a conversation' is close to what I want, but I'd like it to say plainly that it's a phone call with a real person.

unanswered_questions: Who do the couple ring if something goes wrong while they are overseas, outside Melbourne business hours? Is there after-hours support?
Does Wedded Wonderland hold insolvency insurance, and are our deposits protected if a supplier or Wedded Wonderland itself fails?
Whose name are the bookings in when Wedded Wonderland books them, and whose terms apply?
Is the first conversation a phone call, and can I (as a parent paying part) be on it?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee charged: flat, percentage or a mix, and roughly what range? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland receive commissions from the suppliers it books, and will it disclose them? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real honeymoon you've planned that I could see as an example? (deferred business detail)
Are there any perks or extras for couples who book with you? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Insolvency insurance is not compulsory for agents, so ask whoever you book through whether they hold it.
turn_offs_found.why: My turn-off is pages that skip deposits and who is responsible. This one does better than most, but it never uses the word 'deposit', and after telling me to ask about insolvency cover it doesn't say where Wedded Wonderland stands. When it's our money, that silence is what I notice.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Ask a planner | Ask an agent | Why it matters |
turn_offs_found.why: Two identical columns make a long table to read on the iPad for no extra information. One column of questions would be easier on the eye.

would_share_with: My husband, the side-by-side table and 'Questions about what happens when plans change', with my questions on insolvency cover and after-hours contact written underneath
My daughter, the 'Questions about how they are paid' list, so she asks every business the same things in writing

cta_reaction.why: It's a sensible, honest page and 'fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is what I want. But I'd talk to Geoff first, and I'd only go ahead if it leads to a phone call with a real person who can tell me who looks after the children at 2am overseas and whether our deposits are protected.

top_3_changes: In 'Where Wedded Wonderland fits', answer the article's own question 'Who do we contact while we are away?' for Wedded Wonderland (in-trip or after-hours support) and say whether it holds insolvency insurance, only if the source pack supports it; otherwise flag both for the business to confirm.

Collapse the side-by-side table to a single question column plus 'Why it matters' (or add one line saying the columns are deliberately identical), since two identical columns read as an error on a tablet.

Use the word 'deposit' somewhere practical (for example in the payments questions: 'When are deposits due, who holds them, and are they protected?') and, if sourced, say in the closing that the first step is a phone call.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, who is responsible, after-hours contact and a phone call
No invented brand facts; insolvency cover, after-hours support, booking names and first-call format placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Deferred business details (fee model, commissions, ranges, real honeymoons, perks) listed as unanswered questions, not penalised or made must-fix

open_questions.question: Does the source pack support any statement on Wedded Wonderland in-trip or after-hours support, insolvency insurance, or the first step being a phone call? If not, these should be flagged for the business rather than filled.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing to the wedding and honeymoon; relevance is 3 because the page is written to the couple, not to her.
Accessibility for elderly relatives is not relevant to a honeymoon for two, so it was not raised.
The 3-minute budget covered the full article top to bottom, with the FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
